claims.title: Exact rational event-halfspace representation of finite total-variation source-law paths
claims.scope: finite rational source alphabets, a fixed rational initial law, finite horizon, and rational per-step total-variation budgets
assumptions: q_0 equals the declared initial law
each future q_t lies in the probability simplex
TV(q_t,q_{t-1}) is bounded by the declared per-period budget
one event from every complement pair is retained after one simplex coordinate per period is eliminated
nonclaims: active-basis enumeration is not a polynomial-time large-instance guarantee
the declared drift budgets are model inputs unless separately justified

claims.title: Exact primal-dual optimum for time-varying linear costs on a bounded TV drift path
claims.scope: one nonempty bounded rational drift-path polytope and one rational state-cost vector per period
assumptions: the complete bounded path vertex set is enumerated below the configured cap
the dual support search completes below its configured cap
the objective is additive and linear in each period's source law
nonclaims: dual multipliers are not identified with physical energy or force
finite exact arithmetic does not imply practical scalability to arbitrary alphabet and horizon size

claims.title: Independent expanding TV balls upper-bound coupled path cost, with equality under a common state-cost ordering
claims.scope: finite source-law paths with additive rational linear costs and cumulative TV radii derived by triangle inequality
assumptions: the marginal relaxation uses radius R_t=min(1,sum_{s<=t} eta_s)
for the equality statement every period cost vector induces the same weak ordering of source states
canonical TV mass transport uses one consistent tie-breaking order
nonclaims: common ordering is sufficient rather than necessary
a list of individually plausible marginals is not asserted to form one realizable path

claims.title: Exact bounded optimization of precommitted zero-error prefix-code sequences with switching cost
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph, one finite rational drift-path model, deterministic binary prefix codebooks, finite horizon, and rational cost per codebook switch
assumptions: the complete componentwise-undominated deterministic code universe is enumerated below explicit caps
the entire code sequence is fixed before the source path is selected
the code-sequence search exhausts every admissible sequence below the configured sequence and switch caps
the adversarial source path is solved by the exact coupled path optimizer
nonclaims: precommitment is not adaptation to realized symbols or direct observation of the hidden source law
switching cost is an explicit decision-model input rather than a parent-substrate resource inference

claims.title: Two-state reversing costs have coupled value 5/4 while the independent marginal relaxation is 7/4
claims.scope: initial law (1/2,1/2), two periods, per-step TV budget 1/4, and costs (0,1) followed by (1,0)
assumptions: the same source law path must satisfy both period constraints
costs are additive and linear
nonclaims: the numerical gap is specific to the declared finite instance
the result does not imply all changing objectives create a strict coupling gap

claims.title: Uniform K3 rotating-leaf coding gains 1/6 and has switching threshold kappa_c=1/6
claims.scope: complete graph K3, uniform initial law, two periods, per-step TV budget 1/6, and deterministic full binary three-leaf prefix trees
assumptions: the compared rotating sequence uses state-length vectors (1,2,2) and (2,1,2)
the deterministic bounded search exhausts all complete codebooks and two-period sequences
one switch incurs rational penalty kappa
nonclaims: the threshold is specific to the declared coding and drift model
the decision threshold is not a physical phase transition

claims.title: Bounded exact coupled-drift, dual, marginal-gap, and code-sequence audit
claims.scope: the rational one-state, two-state, and K3 instances exercised by the repository test suite
assumptions: all configured path-basis, dual-basis, codebook, and sequence searches complete without truncation
every returned adversarial path is checked period by period against the declared TV budget
nonclaims: bounded tests are not a runtime scalability theorem
CI success is not substituted for the explicit primal, dual, and path receipts
